title: Every categorical localization is essentially surjective
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, $W$ a class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$, and $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a localization in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Then for every object $Y\in\mathcal D$ there are an object $X\in\mathcal C$ and an isomorphism $Q(X)\cong Y$. All categories and functor categories are formed in a common sufficiently large universe.
